properties.title: Abstract Security — Microsoft Entra ID log streams

steps.name: basics
steps.label: Basics
steps.description:
Streams Microsoft Entra ID activity logs — sign-ins, directory audit, provisioning, Identity Protection risk, Microsoft Graph activity — to an Abstract Event Hub.

**This is a TENANT-scope deployment.** One setting covers the entire organisation; adding a subscription later changes nothing here. That is also why **no Azure Policy can manage this**: Entra diagnostic settings are not per-subscription objects, so there is nothing for a `DeployIfNotExists` policy to evaluate. This form *is* the automation.

**You need Security Administrator** on the Entra tenant (plus Attribute Log Administrator if you enable the custom-security-attribute category).

options.text: Tenant-scope deployments require elevated rights and the portal may refuse if your account cannot deploy at tenant scope. The guaranteed path is the CLI: az deployment tenant create --location eastus --template-file templates/tenant/entra-diagnostics.bicep

location.label: Deployment metadata region
location.toolTip: Where the tenant deployment record is stored. Entra logs are not regional, so this does not affect collection.

elements.name: settingName
elements.label: Diagnostic setting name
elements.toolTip: Entra allows multiple diagnostic settings, so this can sit alongside a setting already feeding another SIEM without displacing it.

steps.name: hub
steps.label: Event Hub
steps.description: Where Entra ID logs are delivered.

options.text: Give identity telemetry its OWN hub. Sign-in and Graph-activity volume is high and bursty; a dedicated hub can be partitioned and scaled independently of resource logs, and a backlog on one stream then cannot delay the other.

elements.name: eventHubAuthorizationRuleId
elements.label: Event Hubs authorization rule ID
elements.toolTip: Namespace-level rule with Send rights — the abstractDiagnosticsAuthRuleId output of the Event Hub source template.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be a full namespace-level authorization rule resource ID ending in /authorizationrules/<rule>.

elements.name: eventHubName
elements.label: Event Hub name
elements.toolTip: Must already exist. The source template's default hubSources list (activity/entra/defender) produces abs-prod-entra.

constraints.validationMessage: 1-256 characters: letters, numbers, periods, hyphens, underscores.

steps.name: categories
steps.label: Log categories
steps.description: Which Entra ID streams to collect. Selecting a category your tenant does not license is harmless — it simply produces no records.

elements.name: entraLogCategories
elements.label: Entra ID log categories
elements.toolTip: The default set is what every Abstract Entra detection is built on. MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs is high volume but the single best source for 'what did this token actually do'.

allowedValues.label: AuditLogs — directory changes (users, groups, apps, licences)
NonInteractiveUserSignInLogs — token/client sign-ins on behalf of a user (P1/P2)
ProvisioningLogs — only if you provision via Entra (Workday, ServiceNow…)
ADFSSignInLogs — only if AD FS is in use
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs — every Graph API call (high volume, high value)
EnrichedOffice365AuditLogs — Entra Internet Access + enriched logs enabled
MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs — preview, VERY high volume, first-party service-to-service
B2CRequestLogs — Azure AD B2C tenants only

options.text: Entra diagnostic settings can take UP TO THREE DAYS to deliver their first records — Microsoft documents this. Do not treat an empty hub on day one as a failure, and do not redeploy repeatedly chasing it.

MicrosoftServicePrincipalSignInLogs is first-party Microsoft service-to-service authentication. It is preview, extremely high volume, and Microsoft explicitly advises against acting on it (disabling apps based on it can cause tenant lock-out). Collect it only with a specific reason.

Not listed here: CustomSecurityAttributeAuditLogs. It is configured in a separate section of Entra diagnostic settings, needs the Attribute Log Administrator role, and Microsoft recommends keeping it in its own stream so attribute assignments are not revealed alongside the directory audit log.
